:::{#sol-zero-matrix-practice}

No.
$\matr{Z}$ has three [row](#def-matrix-row)s and two [column](#def-matrix-column)s, so it is $3 \times 2$,
while $\matr{0}_{2 \times 3}$ is $2 \times 3$.
Two [matrices](#def-matrix) of different shapes are not [equal](#def-matrix-equality),
even when every entry of both is $0$.
Instead, $\matr{Z}$ is the [zero matrix](#def-zero-matrix) $\matr{0}_{3 \times 2}$.

:::
